description: UNVERIFIED - PROBABLY INERT. DO NOT SPEND A TEST SLOT ON THIS ON ITS OWN. This pack was authored as 'let a diagonal run in progress last longer' and then failed review. It is kept only because the edit is strictly permissive and costs nothing to carry, and because it becomes live if anyone later raises the continuing-branch distance leash. WHAT IT DOES: one re-aim on the CONTINUING-RUN branch of match::ai::ActionSelectorDiagonalRun::vf5 (0x143e036e0). At 0x143e03a42 the selector calls 0x143daa970(match, slot, 0x21); if the player is already running a diagonal run, 0x143e03a53-0x143e03a60 load the permissive set - cone 40 deg, distance leash C = xmm7 = 8.0 (a register copy, not a pool load), and an ahead-of-ball cap of 15 m in xmm1. The cap is read at 0x143e03a92 (`comiss xmm0, xmm1; ja reject`) with xmm0 = (player.x - ballRef.x) * attackDir. This raises it to 25 m. WHY IT IS ALMOST CERTAINLY INERT (evidence a, emulated): on the SAME branch, the distance gate at 0x143e03c5b compares the squared 2D distance from the player to the game's PREDICTED ball position against maxDist^2, where maxDist = min(8 - 3f, C) + 2. I ran that arithmetic (slice 0x143e03bfb..0x143e03c57) under Unicorn against the PRISTINE image: with C = 8.0 it gives 10.00 / 10.00 / 8.50 / 8.00 / 7.67 / 7.00 / 7.00 at depth 0 / 5 / 9.5 / 11 / 12 / 14 / 20. So an accepted continuing candidate is never more than 10.0 m from the predicted ball position. The two gates are conjunctive - I disassembled every jump between 0x143e03a95 and 0x143e03c5f and the only non-local targets are the reject label 0x143e03fba (`xorps xmm0, xmm0` = score 0). Since |dx| <= euclidean distance, 'ahead of the ball' can only exceed 15 m if the ball travels more than 5 m forward inside the prediction window, and more than 15 m to make 25 m bind. That window is (int)(frameScale*0.1 + 0.5) samples of the ball trajectory table (0x14533ea80 is a two-instruction getter for a global float; 0x144300f00 is the table indexer, max 250 samples), i.e. a small fraction of a second. No football travels 50 m/s, let alone 150 m/s. The premise the pack was written on - 'every diagonal run aborts at the same 15 m point, which is why they all look alike' - is therefore FALSE: runs end on the 7-10 m distance leash, not on this cap. WHAT IS NOT PROVED EITHER WAY: I did not identify [r12+0x25bbc], the reference the 15 m gate measures from (r12 = [match+0x48] via 0x140efd260). If it is the ball's current position, as the surrounding code reads, the argument above is airtight and this pack does nothing. If it is something else that can sit far behind the predicted ball position, the pack could matter. That is the only reason it still exists. IF YOU TEST IT ANYWAY: bundle it with a pack that actually raises the continuing-branch leash, or run it alongside offball-diagonal-band and see whether runs visibly persist longer. Expect no difference. Do NOT believe any claim that it adds variety to run timing. WHO: the attacking side only, both teams equally (0x143d03493 is the sole caller of the selector-manager update 0x143d52470, guarded by `mov ecx,[match+0x3318]; and ecx,1; cmp ecx,[teamAI+8]; jne skip`; no human/CPU test). BYTES: byte-identical in the installed exe and the PRISTINE image; same instruction length; the load at 0x143e03a60 sits between `je 0x143e03a6a` and `jmp 0x143e03a7f`, so it executes only on the already-running path and new-run eligibility cannot be affected; destination 0x145da7de0 is .tls$, non-writable, writers=0; NO pool cell is written. Revert: python tools/exe_patch.py remove tools/data/patches/offball-diagonal-persist-UNVERIFIED-AB.json
